audit.why: 47.28% over 1652 games with the chart Sion/Skill/Kassadin x5 matches the written arc — Sion owns level 1-2, the lane inverts at 3 and never comes back. win[] and the packet chart already agree, so no chart edits.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 spike treats Riftwalk as an unpunishable escape from the moment it exists.
audit.why: Riftwalk is 5s cooldown at rank 1 and only 500 range; it does not become the spam-blink until rank 2 (3.5s) and rank 3 (2s). The 'threat window closes sharply' framing hides a real 5-second punish window right after he blinks.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text and whys[3] now carry the 500 range and the 5s/3.5s rank cooldowns and point at the post-blink window.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page calls Null Sphere a silence in six places, and calls Void Stone a shield that 'blocks' magic damage.
audit.why: Riot's text for Null Sphere is 'dealing damage and interrupting channels' plus a magic-damage shield on Kassadin — no silence. Void Stone is 'takes reduced magic damage and ignores unit collision' — reduction, not immunity, and the unit-collision half is never mentioned even though it means the wave cannot body-block him.
audit.corrected: Null Sphere named, 650 range / 7-9s cooldown, described as an interrupt plus self-shield. Void Stone stated as magic damage REDUCTION plus no unit collision, which is why Sion's physical Q and Roar of the Slayer armour shred are the tools that keep full value and W's magic damage is the one that gets blunted.

audit.whatIsWrong: No mention of his auto-attack reset.
audit.why: Brief flags autoreset-burst-tell: Nether Blade is a 7s empowered auto that also restores mana, so his burst opens on an attack wind-up, not a cast animation. Reading the cast is reading the wrong thing.
It is his only slow and it is a 21s cooldown at rank 1 that additionally requires charging off nearby spellcasts — the longest punishable cooldown in his kit and the page never names it.

edits.before: Kassadin's Q silence reliably interrupts your charge channel now that he has the rotation down — he does not need to fight you, just deny your stun and walk away.
edits.after: Null Sphere is a 650-range orb on 8s that interrupts and shields him from magic — he does not need to fight you, just break your rhythm and walk away.

edits.before: With Riftwalk online he blinks backward every time you start the charge animation; your R travels in a straight line and he sidesteps it trivially.
edits.after: With Riftwalk online he blinks 500 units out when you start the charge, but at rank 1 it is a 5s cooldown — engage in the window right after he burns it.

edits.before: His first AP item pushes his Q-silence trade damage above what your W-shield can absorb, and his Riftwalk cooldown is short enough to dodge your every engage attempt.
edits.after: His first AP item pushes Null Sphere's trade damage above what your W-shield can absorb, and rank-2 Riftwalk on 3.5s dodges nearly every engage attempt you make.

edits.before: Your charged Q is the only threat in this window — Kassadin's passive blocks your W magic damage and his Q silence interrupts your charge, so land the knockup before he silences you.
edits.after: Your charged Q is the only threat here — Void Stone reduces magic damage, so W is blunted but your physical Q and Roar of the Slayer armour shred land in full. Take the knockup early.

edits.before: Kassadin's R (Riftwalk) comes online and he can blink away from every charged Q you attempt — your threat window closes sharply here.
edits.after: Riftwalk comes online — a 500-unit blink, but a 5s cooldown at rank 1, so he escapes one charge and is stuck on the ground for the next few seconds.

edits.before: Land a fully charged Q knockup before Kassadin's Q silence interrupts the channel
edits.after: Land a fully charged Q knockup before Null Sphere lands and breaks the charge

edits.before: Q-silence you mid-charge to cancel your knockup and then trade
edits.after: Break your charge with Null Sphere, then trade with Nether Blade

edits.before: You are a genuine threat at level 1 and level 2 because Kassadin's passive shields magic damage, not your physical charged Q knockup. Walk him toward a wall or tight lane chokepoint, let him push and farm, then start charging Q when he overextends to last-hit. The critical detail: his Q silence is instant and cancels your charge channel if he throws it first — bait the Q by walking forward without charging, then react charge once the silence is on cooldown. W-shield is mostly wasted here since his only poke is the silencing bolt and you gain little from the shield trade. Get a knockup before level 3 if you can; it sets the HP trade in your favour before the matchup inverts.
edits.after: You are a genuine threat at level 1 and level 2: Void Stone only reduces magic damage, so your charged Q knockup and Roar of the Slayer armour shred land at full value. Walk him toward a wall or tight chokepoint, let him push and farm, then start charging Q when he steps up to last-hit. Bait Null Sphere by walking forward without charging, then charge once it is down — it is 9s at rank 1. Watch his auto wind-up rather than his casts: Nether Blade is a 7s empowered attack and that animation is the real tell. Void Stone also means he ignores unit collision, so the wave will not body-block him. Get a knockup before level 3; it sets the HP trade in your favour before the matchup inverts.

edits.before: At level 3 Kassadin has his full base kit and the lane begins slipping away. He will Q-silence you every time you try to charge, reset to range, and the HP advantage you built early starts eroding. Level 6 is the hard line — the moment Riftwalk is available he can blink backward out of any charged Q you attempt and your R (Unstoppable Onslaught) becomes his best friend: he blinks sideways while you travel in a straight line and you overshoot. Play for recalled-and-lost context: if he used Riftwalk aggressively in a fight or to gank, that is your only mid-phase window to punish. Otherwise hold farm and track his roam potential with pings — his level 6 roam down mid is a genuine threat and you have no sprint to match it.
edits.after: At level 3 Kassadin has his full base kit and the lane begins slipping away. Force Pulse is 21s at rank 1 and only fires once he has charged it off nearby spellcasts, so a whiffed cone is a long free window for you. Level 6 is the hard line — the moment Riftwalk is available he can blink out of any charged Q you attempt and your R (Unstoppable Onslaught) becomes his best friend: he blinks sideways while you travel in a straight line and you overshoot. The blink is only 500 units and each repeat costs extra mana, so press him toward a wall rather than in open ground. Otherwise hold farm and track his roams with pings — his level 6 trip down mid is a genuine threat and you have no sprint to match it.

notes: The largest error was systemic: the page called Null Sphere a silence in six fields. Riot's current text is 'dealing damage and interrupting channels' with a magic shield on Kassadin — there is no silence in the kit. I renamed and re-described it but did NOT strengthen or weaken the claim that it stops Sion's Q charge, because neither kit states whether Sion's charge counts as an interruptible channel; that claim is listed in unverified. Void Stone was described as 'shields magic damage' — it is damage reduction, and its unit-collision clause was never used anywhere. No level-chart edits: win[] already matches the packet. currentText.full is null (one of the inherited missing full entries), so all edits are content layer.
